1.content: Create and run a native QuickGUI app with QuickGUI UI. QuickGUI apps are ordinary Go programs. Write components and fine-grained reactive state in Go, then build with CGO_ENABLED=0 . The prebuilt native library is loaded in the same process through purego. Bun runs the CLI for development and packaging.

2.content: macOS 14 or newer Go 1.23 or newer Bun 1.3 or newer Xcode Command Line Tools ( xcode-select --install ) The packaged UI application currently targets macOS. Normal application builds use the prebuilt native host.

3.content: Create a project and launch its native development app.

4.content: The generated main.go imports native for windows and ui for components. Pass the component function directly to WindowOptions.Component . Call native.Run once to start the application event loop.

5.content: The watcher rebuilds your Go source and restarts the development app. The formatter gives long component calls consistent line breaks while preserving ordinary Go syntax. Production bundles are written under dist/darwin-* .

6.content: Understand components and signals . Add styles and conditional options . Explore the component reference .

9.content: main.go starts native.Run and creates a window. Components and children blocks share the func() signature and declare their children in order, without returning a node. Split larger applications into ordinary Go packages.

11.content: Use github.com/egoist/quickgui/go/native for windows and platform services, github.com/egoist/quickgui/go/ui for UI, and github.com/egoist/quickgui/go/reactive for owners and contexts. @quickgui/cli is a development dependency. Pin the Go SDK and CLI to compatible release versions.

12.content: Use QuickGUI UI reactivity to render retained native UI. Go components create retained native nodes. Signals subscribe individual bindings to the state they read.
12.keywords: go signal component reactivity lifecycle router

13.content: Every component uses func() , including window roots, routes, conditional branches, and children blocks. It declares zero or more children without returning a node. Components run once when mounted. UI calls inside a children block attach to that block’s parent. Use normal Go if and for for static construction; use ui.Show or ui.For when a signal must change the child structure.

14.content: Pass an accessor for changing text or properties. Calling count() while constructing a string captures its current value; placing the call in func() string keeps it reactive. Event handlers batch writes automatically. Use ui.Batch for a group of writes elsewhere, and ui.CreateMemo for derived values.

15.content: WindowOptions.Component creates one reactive root per window. Closing the window disposes its nodes and effects. Register resource cleanup with ui.OnCleanup . For background work, ui.Async delivers its result back to the UI goroutine and cancels when its component is disposed.

16.content: Capture native.CurrentWindow() while the component is mounting, then use the captured window in callbacks. Do not look it up from an unrelated goroutine. Window events and native requests expose asynchronous callbacks.

17.content: Declare routes with ui.Route and ui.Layout . A layout mounts its matched child with ui.Outlet . Read parameters with ui.UseParams , or navigate with ui.UseRouter .

18.content: Lay out and style native nodes with familiar properties. Primitives accept style options and children directly. Compound parts accept a ui.Style through ui.PartProps .
18.keywords: style layout flexbox grid color hover

19.content: Use functional options for short declarations. Reuse a record with ui.WithStyle(style) . Numeric lengths are logical pixels; strings also accept percentages. A numeric zero is meaningful; nil omits the value. Run bun run fmt to wrap long component calls consistently.

20.content: Set Display("flex") , choose a direction, then declare sizing and alignment. A scrolling flex child usually needs MinHeight(0) or MinWidth(0) so it can shrink.

21.content: Grid uses familiar track strings. Place children explicitly when auto-placement is not enough.

22.content: Typography inherits through the node tree. Colors accept hex, rgb() / rgba() , or packed RGBA values. Pass color and numeric accessors for reactive paint or size changes.

23.content: ui.Hover , ui.Active , and ui.Focus describe interaction styles. ui.When applies options while a reactive condition is true and restores previous values when it turns false. Use ui.DisabledStyle and ui.SelectedStyle for those interaction states. Children remain mounted.

24.content: Choose between primitives and accessible compound components. QuickGUI combines unstyled primitives with accessible compound controls. Compose both through ordinary Go functions.
24.keywords: view text button tabs checkbox unstyled

25.content: Start with ui.View , ui.Text , ui.Button , and ui.Input . Options and text can be passed directly. A func() { ... } argument groups multiple children under the current parent.

26.content: Compound families expose parts such as ui.Tabs.Root , ui.Tabs.List , and ui.Tabs.Panel . The core handles roles, keyboard navigation, focus, and control state. Create a part inside its root’s children callback so its context exists.

27.content: A controlled value is an accessor; its callback stores the value accepted by the control. Use a default value to let the component own its state. Optional scalar values use pointers, while multiple selections use slices.

28.content: The reference covers forms, pickers, layout and data, overlays, menus, and routing. examples/components contains all 42 original gallery demos, including a 5,000-row table and lazy tree. The separate examples/swift-ui gallery demonstrates native SwiftUI hosting.

32.content: Field.Root associates a label, control, description, and error. Set Required , Invalid , and ValidationMessage from application state. ValidationMode and ValidationDebounceTime configure when the core requests validation; your application owns the validation rule.

33.content: Checkboxes accept bool or ui.CheckedIndeterminate through ui.CheckedState . Radio groups keep one value; checkbox and toggle groups can keep several. Read-only controls remain distinct from disabled controls.

34.content: Declare picker options through PickerSourceProps.Items . Select uses a chosen value; Combobox combines text filtering and selection; Autocomplete accepts free-form input. Multiple pickers use Values and OnValuesChange .

35.content: Plain buttons accept ui.OnClick(func() { ... }) . Use ui.OnClickEvent when you need *native.Event . Compound callbacks use typed values and include the native event when relevant. Keep UI state updates on the UI goroutine; use ui.Async for background work.

37.content: A popover composes a trigger, positioner, and popup. The side is a preference; the core resolves collisions. Read the result through ui.UsePopoverPlacement inside the root.

38.content: Create modal content under Dialog.Portal . Dialog.Title and Dialog.Description provide its accessible name and description. AlertDialog adds confirmation semantics. Controlled roots receive both the next open state and its reason.

39.content: ui.SystemPopover hosts its body in an operating-system popover. Specify its logical width and height, then declare ordinary QuickGUI children.

40.content: Native dialogs use asynchronous callbacks. Capture the parent window while rendering and pass it explicitly to the request. A canceled open panel returns Canceled: true .

41.content: Mount real SwiftUI controls inside a QuickGUI UI application. The ui.SwiftUI family embeds real macOS controls in a Go application. Ordinary QuickGUI components work without it.
41.keywords: swiftui host slider toggle picker native

42.content: Create controls inside ui.SwiftUI.Host . The host defines the native view boundary and can size itself from its content.

43.content: Available controls include Button, Slider, Toggle, ProgressView, Stepper, TextField, SecureField, Picker, SegmentedControl, DatePicker, ColorPicker, and Gauge. Their platform appearance comes from macOS.

44.content: Bind an accessor and store the value returned by the native callback. A SwiftUI control and a QuickGUI node can share the same signal. DatePicker uses Unix timestamps in milliseconds.

45.content: MatchContents: true sizes both axes intrinsically. Use ui.SwiftUIMatchContents{Vertical: true} for an intrinsic height with an application-defined width in PartProps.Style .

46.content: SwiftUI hosting requires macOS. The prebuilt native host includes the bridge; your Go application still builds without CGO. Native styles can vary with the operating-system version.

47.content: Style SwiftUI controls and host QuickGUI content back inside them. SwiftUI modifiers style native controls. Reverse hosting puts an ordinary QuickGUI subtree inside SwiftUI.

Create and run a native QuickGUI app with QuickGUI UI. QuickGUI apps are ordinary Go programs. Write components and fine-grained reactive state in Go, then build with CGO_ENABLED=0 . Create controls inside ui.SwiftUI.Host . The host defines the native view boundary and can size itself from its content.

entry is the Go package to build. The configuration file is evaluated by the Bun CLI. It is not part of the running application.

Every component uses func() , including window roots, routes, conditional branches, and children blocks. It declares zero or more children without returning a node. Components run once when mounted. UI calls inside a children block attach to that block’s parent. Use normal Go if and for for static construction; use ui.Show or ui.For when a signal must change the child structure.

Native dialogs use asynchronous callbacks. Capture the parent window while rendering and pass it explicitly to the request. A canceled open panel returns Canceled: true .
